stem: There are 10 persons among whom two are brothers. The total number of ways in which these persons can be seated around a round table so that exactly one person sits between the brothers, is equal to:
_note: Derived independently before consulting the printed key: choose the person seated between the brothers in 8 ways, order the brothers in \(2!\) ways, then treat the 3-person block plus the remaining 7 as 8 units round a circle, \((8-1)! = 7!\). Total \(8 \times 2 \times 7! = 16 \times 7! = 2 \times 8! = 2! \times 8!\). Cross-checked by probability: fixing one brother, the other has 9 seats of which 2 are one seat away, and \(80640/9! = 2/9\). Printed key: B. AGREE.

stem: The number of arrangements of the letters of the word BANANA in which two N's do not appear adjacently
_note: Derived independently before consulting the printed key: BANANA has B, three A's and two N's, so total \(6!/(3!\,2!) = 60\); treating NN as one unit gives \(5!/3! = 20\); hence \(60 - 20 = 40\). Printed key: C. AGREE. Note option B (60) is the total-arrangements distractor.

stem: The number of ways in which 5 male and 2 female members of a committee can be seated around a round table so that the two females are not seated together is
_note: Derived independently before consulting the printed key: total circular arrangements \((7-1)! = 720\); the two females together give \((6-1)! \times 2! = 240\); hence \(720 - 240 = 480\). Cross-checked by direct construction: seat the 5 males in \(4! = 24\) ways and place the females in 2 of the 5 gaps, \({}^{5}P_{2} = 20\), giving \(24 \times 20 = 480\). Printed key: D. AGREE. Option C (720) is the total-arrangements distractor.

ANSWER-KEY DISAGREEMENT (flagged for the cross-check pass, not repaired here). \({}^{56}P_{r+6} \div {}^{54}P_{r+3} = \frac{56!}{(50-r)!} \times \frac{(51-r)!}{54!} = 56 \times 55 \times (51-r) = 3080(51-r)\). Setting \(3080(51-r) = 30800\) gives \(51-r = 10\), so \(r = 41\). The printed key gives 45, and \(r = 45\) yields \(56 \times 55 \times 6 = 18480\), not 30800. So either the key should read 41, or the stem's ratio should read 18480 : 1. Stem transcribed exactly as printed.
solution: [Textbook answer-key error: the printed key gives \(r = 45\). The ratio \({}^{56}P_{r+6} : {}^{54}P_{r+3}\) reduces to \(56 \times 55 \times (51-r) = 3080(51-r)\), so setting it equal to \(30800\) gives \(51 - r = 10\) and \(r = 41\). Checked by direct computation: \(r = 41\) yields exactly \(30800\), while the key's \(r = 45\) yields \(18480\). Either the key should read 41, or the stem's ratio should read \(18480 : 1\).]

stem: A student finds 7 books of his interest, but can borrow only three books. He wants to borrow Chemistry part II book only if Chemistry Part I can also be borrowed. Find the number of ways he can choose three books that he wants to borrow.
_note: UNSTATED CONVENTION (flagged, not forced). Read strictly, 'II only if I' bars only the case II-without-I, giving \({}^{7}C_{3} - {}^{5}C_{2} = 35 - 10 = 25\). The printed key 15 corresponds to the stricter reading in which the two Chemistry parts are taken as a package — either both (\({}^{5}C_{1} = 5\)) or neither (\({}^{5}C_{3} = 10\)) — which additionally bars I-without-II. The stem does not say which is intended.
solution: [Textbook ambiguity, not a straightforward error: the printed key of 15 requires reading "Chemistry II only if Chemistry I" as a PACKAGE — both papers or neither — which additionally bars taking Chemistry I without Chemistry II. Read strictly, the condition bars only II-without-I, giving \(35 - 10 = 25\). The stem states only the one-way condition. The answer above follows the strict reading and names the alternative.]

_note: ANSWER-KEY QUERY (flagged for the cross-check pass). The two groups are distinguishable (car vs train), so the car group may hold 3, 4, 5 or 6 friends and the count is \({}^{9}C_{3} + {}^{9}C_{4} + {}^{9}C_{5} + {}^{9}C_{6} = 84 + 126 + 126 + 84 = 420\). The printed key stops at \({}^{9}C_{3} + {}^{9}C_{4} + {}^{9}C_{5} = 336\), which appears to drop the \({}^{9}C_{6}\) term.
solution: [Textbook answer-key error: the printed key sums \({}^9C_3 + {}^9C_4 + {}^9C_5 = 336\). Because the car group and the train group are distinguishable, \({}^9C_6\) belongs in the sum as well, giving \({}^9C_3 + {}^9C_4 + {}^9C_5 + {}^9C_6 = 420\). The key appears to have dropped the final term.]
